Job Summary:

The Geisinger Research Data Core is responsible for transforming and managing clinical and genomic data for research use. As part of a collaborative and multidisciplinary team, this position develops and maintains data systems and pipelines that support research applications and the use of large-scale clinical and genomic datasets. The role provides key insight into data architecture, data modeling, and application development and engages in all aspects of the development life cycle as needed for each project to be successful.

We are seeking a skilled Senior Data Engineer with experience in cloud-based data platforms, particularly the Databricks platform and AWS. The ideal candidate will be responsible for modeling clinical data within the Databricks environment, developing and maintaining scalable data pipelines, and modernizing legacy ETL processes for cloud environments. The position will also support data quality, performance optimization, monitoring, and general Databricks computing needs for research and analytical applications.

Job Duties:

- Designs, develops, and maintains PySpark and SQL data pipelines for transforming clinical data for research use.

- Develops and maintains data models for clinical and other research data within the Databricks environment.
- Reviews, analyzes, modifies, creates, debugs, designs, and tests data ingestion and processing pipelines using modern development methodologies and tools.
- Defines and optimizes data warehouse schemas and data models to support efficient querying, storage, and analytical workflows.
- Ensures scalability, reliability, and maintainability of data pipelines and data architecture supporting large clinical and research datasets.
- Implements and monitors data quality checks and validation processes to ensure accuracy, completeness, and integrity of data throughout the pipeline.
- Troubleshoots and optimizes Spark and SQL workloads, data pipelines, and Databricks compute resources to improve performance and reliability.
- Modernizes existing on-premises Microsoft SQL Server ETL processes by designing and implementing equivalent cloud-based data pipelines and workflows in Databricks.
- Provides general Databricks computing support, including assisting users with compute resource selection, troubleshooting, and optimization of Spark and SQL workloads.
- Participates in design and application architecture discussions and assists in the development and documentation of technical approaches and solutions for team stakeholders.
- Responsible for the process, life cycle and creation of the software to assist users in completing a computer task or program.
- Implements code and documents all system changes based on assignments and timelines.
- Develops and follows department coding and user interface guidelines.
- Provides code review, testing, debugging, technical documentation, general testing instructions, go-live planning, assistance in go-live moves, and post-live support.
- Communicates all progress, roadblocks, and issues to the team and management in a timely manner.
- Collaborates with team members to identify and resolve issues, improve system performance, and ensure code quality.
- Provides training and documentation to team members on new development assignments.
- Trains and mentors staff members.
- Assists in the development and documentation of a technical approach for a solution to the team stakeholders.

Work is typically performed in an office environment. Accountable for satisfying all job specific obligations and complying with all organization policies and procedures. The specific statements in this profile are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements considered necessary to successfully perform the job.

*Relevant experience may be a combination of related work experience and degree obtained (Associate’s Degree = 2 years; Bachelor’s Degree = 4 years; Master’s Degree = 6 years).

Position Details:

Requirements:

- Proven experience with Databricks and cloud-based data engineering platforms.
- Strong experience with SQL and Python/PySpark for developing and optimizing data processing pipelines.
- Experience with Apache Spark or other distributed data processing technologies.
- Experience designing and implementing data models and data warehouse schemas for large-scale datasets.
- Experience developing, maintaining, or modernizing ETL processes and data pipelines.
- Experience working with relational databases and SQL Server
- Experience migrating or modernizing on-premises ETL processes is preferred.
- Familiarity with AWS cloud services and cloud-based data architectures.
- Experience with data quality, validation, monitoring, logging, and troubleshooting practices.
- Understanding of data pipeline performance optimization and scalable data processing.
- Excellent communication skills to convey progress, roadblocks, technical issues, and solutions to team members and management.
- Ability to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team and collaborate with technical and research stakeholders.

Minimum of 10 years-Related work experience (Required)

summary: Lead and coordinate Real-World Data engineering delivery across ingestion, engineering, and distribution, including roadmap planning, prioritization, dependencies, governance, and value tracking. description:
When our values align, there's no limit to what we can achieve.

At Parexel, we all share the same goal - to improve the world's health. From clinical trials to regulatory, consulting, and market access, every clinical development solution we provide is underpinned by something special - a deep conviction in what we do.

Each of us, no matter what we do at Parexel, contributes to the development of a therapy that ultimately will benefit a patient. We take our work personally, we do it with empathy and we're committed to making a difference.

Parexel is in the business of improving the world’s health. We do this by providing a suite of biopharmaceutical services that help clients across the globe transform scientific discoveries into new treatments.  We believe in our values, _Patients First, Quality, Respect, Empowerment & Accountability._

This role will work within our innovative _Data & Technology group_ that continues to evolve to meet business needs, fuel Parexel's growth and enable improved support for stakeholders, including customers and ultimately patients, who will benefit from Parexel's integrated processes and systems.

This role can be based in the _UK_, _Poland or Romania_ and can be _fully home based_ and _remote working_ anywhere in any of _these locations only_.

As t _he Director, Data Engineering -_ _RWD_ is a domain-aligned technical execution leader with predominant experience in life sciences, clinical research, and Real-World Data, responsible for orchestrating and driving delivery across Data Ingestion, Data Engineering, and Data Distribution for RWD and related enterprise data products.

This is a strong individual contributor role with no direct line management authority, however it requires strong matrixed leadership, technical credibility, and influence across data engineering, Clinical Operations, Commercial, and broader business stakeholders to ensure that life sciences data priorities are translated into executable plans and delivered with consistency, transparency, regulatory awareness, and measurable impact.

You will partner with Data and Technology, the Data and Analytics CoE, Clinical Operations, Commercial, business domain stakeholders, platform teams, governance partners, and delivery teams to translate life sciences and Real-World Data needs into executable engineering priorities.

You will lead intake management, roadmap shaping, prioritization, dependency management, stakeholder alignment, delivery governance, and value tracking, while establishing clear ownership, managing dependencies, coordinating delivery sequencing, and ensuring trusted, high-quality, governed, and reusable data assets are available for analytics, AI enablement, operational reporting, regulatory-aligned use cases, and sponsor-facing distribution.

What You'll Lead:

RWD Data Domain Engineering & Orchestration

- Act as the domain-aligned engineering coordination / orchestration lead for Real-World Data in a life sciences context, connecting clinical research, operational, and commercial priorities to executable plans across ingestion, transformation, curation, and distribution.
- Drive delivery across Data Ingestion, Data Engineering, and Data Distribution teams, ensuring clear scope, sequencing, dependency management, and execution follow-through.
- Provide technical leadership for scalable RWD pipelines, lakehouse design, architecture, data quality controls, metadata practices, and reusable data product patterns.

Matrixed Execution Leadership & Cross-Functional Orchestration

- Serve as the primary matrixed coordination point between RWD stakeholders, Clinical Operations, Commercial, life sciences business domain owners, architects, engineers, governance teams, analytics teams, and downstream consumers.
- Lead intake, prioritization, roadmap shaping, delivery planning, and operating cadence for RWD data initiatives, balancing urgency, capacity, quality, risk, compliance, and business value.
- Influence execution across teams without direct authority by building shared understanding, clarifying tradeoffs, resolving blockers, and driving commitment to agreed outcomes.

Technical Leadership, Team Enablement & Delivery Discipline

- Coordinate across data engineering teams and stakeholders to align expectations for technical quality, execution discipline, stakeholder engagement, and delivery accountability.

- Champion capability development in cloud data engineering, Azure Databricks, lakehouse architecture, CI/CD, SQL, Python, data observability, governance, and secure data distribution.

- Track delivered outputs against planned KPIs and expected value measures to ensure the data capability delivered the intended business, operational, clinical, and stakeholder outcomes.

What We're Looking For:

Skills:

- Deep technical expertise in enterprise data engineering, including ingestion patterns, transformation frameworks, lakehouse architecture, medallion design, data quality, metadata management, and operational support.

- Strong matrixed leadership and orchestration skills, with demonstrated ability to influence and align technical/data engineering, Clinical Operations, Commercial, governance, analytics, and business stakeholders without relying on direct reporting relationships.

- Predominant experience with life sciences data environments, including Real-World Data, clinical research data, healthcare data, regulated data environments, GxP expectations, privacy controls, sponsor/client needs, and data governance.

- Strong business stakeholder engagement skills, with experience aligning technology capabilities to clinical, operational, commercial, and sponsor-facing outcomes

- Hands-on knowledge of cloud data platforms and engineering tools, particularly Azure Databricks, Azure Data Lake, SQL, Python, Spark, APIs, orchestration frameworks, CI/CD, and monitoring practices.

- Ability to apply product- and program-management discipline, structured delivery discipline, and coordination/orchestration discipline to data engineering delivery, including intake management, roadmap development, backlog shaping, prioritization, dependency management, delivery tracking, success measures, and stakeholder-ready communications.

- Proven ability to manage cross-team dependencies, delivery risks, prioritization tradeoffs, capacity constraints, and competing stakeholder expectations in a matrixed organization.

Knowledge and Experience

- Strong advanced level experience of IT, data, analytics, or technology, with a predominant focus on life sciences, clinical research, healthcare data, RWD, or regulated data environments, including significant hands-on leadership in enterprise data engineering, integration, cloud platforms, and data delivery.

- Previous high level experience leading complex data engineering, data delivery, or analytics platform initiatives in life sciences, clinical research, healthcare, or RWD environments through matrixed leadership, including coordination across ingestion, engineering, distribution, Clinical Operations, Commercial, governance, analytics, and business stakeholders.

- Strong previous technical leadership or matrixed delivery leadership experience, including:

- Successfully developing and implementing applications in new computing architecture environments using innovative technologies.

- Influencing technical and business teams across multiple project lifecycle phases; cross-functional leadership across technical, clinical, commercial, governance, and analytics stakeholders is highly desirable.

- Leading resources to achieve goals across multiple projects.

- Developing efficient and effective solutions to complex business challenges.

- Experience working directly with business and operational stakeholders to translate business needs into technology priorities, delivery plans, success measures, and realized outcomes.

- Experience in life sciences, clinical research, healthcare, RWD, or regulated data environments is expected; experience with clinical trial operations, sponsor-facing data delivery, regulatory-aware analytics, or commercial life sciences data is strongly preferred.

Education

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field (required)

In return we will be able to offer you a structured career pathway and encouragement to develop within the role including awareness and understanding of the industry.  You will be well supported and in return for your hard work you will be rewarded with a competitive base salary, bonus, car allowance and holiday as well as other leading benefits you would expect with a top company in the CRO Industry.

description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

## Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Insights & Intelligence (i2) is reimagining decision making at Northrop Grumman. As part of our Chief Information & Digital Office (CIDO), i2 works with all enterprise domains and businesses to drive our data, analytics & AI transformation.

As a leader, you will manage a team of data and software engineers working across critical domains of the business. In this role, you will directly influence how we build our Databricks enterprise lakehouse and our culture of engineering excellence that enables the team to develop reliable data systems. You will have the opportunity to grow as an engineering leader, influencing the technical architecture and code standards on the team along with the technical roadmap and its execution.

This position is supporting the corporate office in Falls Church, VA. We will consider virtual telecommuter candidates.

Key responsibilities:

- Define and maintain a data engineering roadmap; align technical priorities with business objectives and the Northrop Grumman data strategy.
- Build and lead a high-performing, collaborative team; mentoring engineers on design patterns, code quality, data architecture, and career development.
- Champion clean, modular architecture and enforce engineering best practices.
- Drive end-to-end delivery of data pipelines in Databricks, ensuring reliability, scalability, and performance while meeting roadmap milestones.
- Collaborate with leaders and teams across various functions, including business management, business development, facilities, human resources, supply chain, and manufacturing.

Basic Qualifications:

- Must have, at minimum, a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
- Must have a minimum of 8 years of experience in software or data engineering with a relevant Bachelors Degree OR 6 years of experience in software or data engineering with a relevant Masters Degree.
- Must have a minimum of 2 years of experience in people management leading engineering teams.
- Proficiency with Databricks (or comparable modern data lakehouse platforms), cloud services (AWS), and data pipelines.
- Demonstrated skill in managing technical teams, process excellence, and meeting roadmap deliverables.
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with a demonstrated ability to influence both technical and executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Master’s degree or PhD in Engineering or related field.
- Deep domain expertise in one or more of the following areas: Finance, Supply Chain, Human Resources, or Manufacturing

Primary Level Salary Range: $133,200.00 - $199,800.00

The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions.

Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. Data Engineering Strategy and Architecture

Data Integration, Ingestion, and Modernization

Operational Excellence and Engineering Standards

Data Governance, Security, and Quality

- Support the delivery of governed, trusted, and documented data assets for enterprise reporting, analytics, applications, and artificial intelligence initiatives.

Stakeholder Partnership and Planning

- Develop and maintain the Data Engineering roadmap, aligning technology priorities with business, regulatory, operational, and strategic objectives.

Skills

AWS DMS → GCP-native CDC solutions

Define migration phases, technical dependencies, risks and rollback strategies.

Lead architecture reviews and technical design discussions.

Amazon Athena

AWS DMS

Google Pub/Sub

Dataflow / Apache Beam

BigQuery

Cloud Storage

Design high-volume event ingestion, enrichment and transformation pipelines.

Implement event-driven architectures and appropriate delivery guarantees.

Optimize streaming pipelines for latency, throughput and scalability.

Design BigQuery streaming ingestion patterns.

Python

SQL

BigQuery

dbt

The Director will lead the Data Engineering team and work closely with executives, business leaders, analytics teams, application teams, vendors, and other technology functions. This leader will translate business needs into practical data solutions, establish priorities based on business value, and communicate technical concepts, risks, dependencies, and recommendations in clear business terms.

- Lead the Data Engineering team, including technical direction, coaching, prioritization, performance management, and accountability for delivery.

description:
We are an MIT-born, venture-backed Silicon Valley startup building Engineering General Intelligence (EGI)—an AI Copilot for design and manufacturing. Our mission is to fundamentally reinvent how physical products are designed and built, dramatically accelerating the pace of product development.

As an Individual Contributor on the Data Studio team, you will play a key role in transforming raw customer data into structured, high-fidelity datasets that power model training, evaluation, and customer delivery. This role is deeply hands-on and sits at the intersection of product, research, and engineering. You will apply your mechanical engineering and manufacturing expertise to create data pipelines, labeling workflows, reference models, and quality checks that ensure the accuracy and reliability of our AI systems. Mechanical engineering or manufacturing design experience is essential; candidates without this background will not be considered.

\\n

Key Responsibilities

- 1\. Data Creation, Processing & Quality
- Ingest, clean, transform, and structure customer and internally generated engineering data for AI training and inference.
- Design and build high-quality mechanical components and assemblies in CAD to serve as authoritative ground truth for evaluating and training AI systems.
- Produce labeled datasets, reference designs, annotations, exploded views, sequences, and other engineering artifacts that encode real-world reasoning.
- Apply engineering judgment to define and assess output quality across datasets.
- Continuously refine standards for metadata, annotation, and model quality, maintaining a living “definition of quality” for ME datasets.

- 2\. Workflow & Tooling Contributions
- Collaborate with Product Managers to shape tooling used for annotation, data correction, model-output review, and pipeline automation.
- Provide detailed feedback on tool usability, workflow efficiency, and automation opportunities.
- Help develop scalable, repeatable data processes that improve throughput and data consistency.

- 3\. Cross-Functional Collaboration
- Partner closely with engineering and research teams to understand model data requirements, failure modes, and areas needing new data.
- Influence model behavior by supplying representative engineering examples and ground-truth mechanical designs.
- Partner with customer-facing teams to translate domain requirements, industry standards, and customer data schemas into actionable dataset specifications.
- Serve as a subject matter expert on mechanical engineering formats, CAD standards, manufacturing practices, and design artifacts.

description:
## About Invisible

Invisible Technologies makes AI work. Our end-to-end AI platform structures messy data, automates digital workflows, deploys agentic solutions, measures outcomes, and integrates human expertise where it matters most.

Our platform cleans, labels, and structures company data so it is ready for AI. It adapts models to each business and adds human expertise when needed, the same approach we have used to improve models for more than 80% of the world’s top AI companies, including Microsoft, AWS, and Cohere.

Our successes span industries, from supply chain automation for Swiss Gear to AI-enabled naval simulations with SAIC, and validating NBA draft picks for the Charlotte Hornets.

Profitable for more than half a decade, Invisible reached $134M in revenue and ranked as the number two fastest growing AI company on the 2024 Inc. 5000. In September 2025, we raised $100M in growth capital to accelerate our mission of making AI actually work in the enterprise and to advance our platform technology.

## About the Role

We're looking for a Director of Engineering to set the technical strategy for Data Labs, the team that builds the benchmarking systems, data pipelines, and RL environments behind our AI training engagements. The frontier labs and enterprises we work with are changing how they train, evaluate, and deploy models every quarter. Your job is to see where that market is going and make sure Data Labs is built for it before our clients ask.

You'll decide which capabilities we invest in, which we standardize into platform, and which we leave to individual engagements. You'll track how training methods, evaluation practices, and data needs are shifting across the industry, and turn that into a technical roadmap and a point of view our commercial and research teams can sell against.

You'll lead a group of engineering managers, forward deployed engineers (FDEs), and senior ICs, and partner closely with applied research, product, and go-to-market leadership. This is a hands-on strategic role. You won't spend much time writing code, but you'll stay close enough to the technical work to make and defend hard architectural calls, and close enough to clients to know which calls matter.

## What You'll Do

### Technical Strategy & Roadmap

- Own the multi-year technical strategy for Data Labs, and translate it into a roadmap tied to where the AI training and evaluation market is heading.
- Decide where to build shared platform versus engagement-specific solutions, weighing reuse against team autonomy so platforms speed teams up rather than creating over-dependency.
- Set architectural direction for benchmarking infrastructure, data pipelines, and RL environments so they stay reproducible, portable across client deployments, and ready for the next generation of training methods.
- Anticipate technical shifts 6–18 months out, such as new post-training techniques, agentic evaluation, and synthetic data, and place the bets that keep Invisible ahead of them.
- Set expectations for how AI is used in design reviews and day-to-day engineering work.

### Market Intelligence & Competitive Positioning

- Build a clear, current view of how frontier labs and enterprises are training, evaluating, and deploying models, and what that means for the data and infrastructure they'll need from us.
- Track the competitive landscape across AI data, evaluation, and RL environment providers, and help define where Invisible differentiates.
- Turn client signals, research developments, and market trends into investment recommendations for executive leadership.
- Partner with product and commercial teams to shape new offerings, pricing logic, and the technical story behind them.

### Evaluation & Data Strategy

- Define Invisible's point of view on benchmarking and evaluation, including pre- and post-engagement comparisons, capability gap analyses, and regression tracking.
- Make sure evaluation design ties to client-defined success metrics, validate automated checks against human judgment, and be explicit about what each approach can't see.
- Identify reusable data assets, frameworks, and pipelines that become durable advantages and improve margins across engagements.
- Shape practices for data licensing, privacy, and contamination risk as a strategic differentiator, not just a compliance requirement.

### Client & Executive Engagement

- Represent engineering in executive conversations, strategic client relationships, and pre-sales, translating technical reality into clear, honest narratives.
- Act as a trusted technical advisor to client research and engineering leaders, bringing back what you learn to inform the roadmap.
- Help leaders weigh client-specific asks against broader platform and business goals, with clear short- and long-term paths.

### Organizational Leadership

- Lead and grow an engineering org of multiple teams, including engineering managers, senior managers, FDEs, and Staff+ ICs.
- Coach managers to build sound technical judgment and strategic awareness in their teams.
- Build hiring pipelines that reinforce a rigorous, client-focused, strategy-aware engineering culture.
- Make sure the org has the planning, quality, and operational practices it needs to execute on the strategy reliably, delegating day-to-day delivery to strong managers.

## What We're Looking For

- 10+ years in software engineering, with significant experience building ML or AI systems.
- 5+ years in engineering leadership, including experience managing managers across multiple teams.
- A track record of setting multi-year technical strategy and making platform investment decisions that paid off commercially.
- Deep, current understanding of the AI training and evaluation landscape, including how frontier labs and enterprises approach fine-tuning, RLHF/RLAIF, and evaluation methodology.
- Hands-on familiarity with LLM training pipelines, deep enough to make and defend architectural decisions.
- Experience building benchmarking, data curation, or RL infrastructure that produced measurable client outcomes.
- Ability to read market and competitive signals and turn them into a technical roadmap and a clear product point of view.
- Strong cross-functional partnership with applied research, product, and commercial teams.
- Excellent executive communication, and confidence acting as a technical advisor in client and pre-sales conversations.

## Nice to Have

- Prior experience at an AI services firm, applied research consultancy, frontier lab, or enterprise AI product company.
- A visible point of view on the AI data and evaluation market, such as talks, writing, or open-source work.
- Familiarity with data licensing, synthetic data generation, or contamination detection involving client data.
- Experience shaping new product lines or service offerings from a technical foundation.
- Experience leading an org through rapid growth or significant change.

What’s In It For You

Invisible is committed to fair and competitive pay, ensuring that compensation reflects both market conditions and the value each team member brings. Our salary structure accounts for regional differences in cost of living while maintaining internal equity.

For this position, the annual salary will include a 20% annual bonus and an additional incentive structure. The base salary range for SF/NY are:

Salary Range

$252,000—$300,000 USD

You can find more information about our geographic pay tiers [here](https://invisibletech.ai/compensation-and-pay-tiers). During the interview process, your Invisible Talent Acquisition Partner will confirm which tier applies to your location. For candidates outside the U.S., compensation is adjusted to reflect local market conditions and cost of living.

*Bonuses and equity are included in all full-time offers. Final compensation is determined by a combination of factors, including location, job-related experience, skills, knowledge, internal pay equity, and overall market conditions. Because of this, every offer is unique. Additional details on total compensation and benefits will be discussed during the hiring process.

## What It's Like to Work at Invisible:

At Invisible, we’re not just redefining work—we’re reinventing it. We operate at the intersection of advanced AI and human ingenuity, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible to unlock productivity and scale. Ownership is at the core of everything we do. Here, you won’t just execute tasks—you’ll build, innovate, and shape the future alongside world-class clients pushing the boundaries of AI.

We expect bold ideas, relentless drive, and the ability to turn ambiguity into opportunity. The pace is fast, the challenges are big, and the growth is unmatched. We’re not for everyone, and we’re okay with that. If you’re looking for predictable routines, this isn’t the place for you. But if you’re driven to create, thrive in dynamic environments, and want a front-row seat to the AI revolution, you’ll fit right in.
